subject: Post-call: Emergency support auth, retention windows & residency clarifications
messages:
From: Alex Rivera <alex.rivera@finsecure.io>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>
Cc: LegalOps <legal@finsecure.io>
Date: Mon, 21 Jun 2027 10:12:00 -0700
Subject: Follow-up from today's discovery — emergency support & data requirements

Evelyn, thanks for the call this morning. Quick recap and a few clarifying asks so my team can evaluate Redwood against our procurement criteria. Appreciate a short written confirmation on each item where possible.

Summary (FinSecure constraints):
- PII scope: We store customer names, emails, hashed SSNs (tokenized), and some device identifiers. We'll attach a short inventory.
- Data residency: Primary requirement is that inference and any persisted customer artifacts remain within the US (multi-region within US is OK).
- Retention: Default retention must be configurable per-tenant; legal requires a max retention of 30 days for request/response logs that contain PII; anonymized token logs may be kept longer for ops.
- Support access: Support engineers must not have standing access to raw PII. We need: role-based break-glass that logs every session, just-in-time approvals from a named FinSecure approver, and per-session tokenized masking.
- Logging & audit: Immutable audit trail for access requests, approvals, and data exports for 3 years.

Attached is a PII inventory (FinSecure_PII_inventory.xlsx). Can you confirm which of these are considered "persisted artifacts" by Redwood, what level of masking Redwood can do server-side, and whether you can support JIT break-glass approval tied to our SSO/Okta?

We are working on an initial security questionnaire that Legal will send; for now this is to help us size the procurement and any needed architecture review.

Thanks — Alex
Alex Rivera
Head of Platform Security, FinSecure

From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>
To: Alex Rivera <alex.rivera@finsecure.io>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 21 Jun 2027 14:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up from today's discovery — emergency support & data requirements

Alex — great speaking earlier. Quick answers inline below, then proposed next steps.

- PII scope: Received your inventory; thanks. Redwood treats request payloads and inference outputs as transient by default unless a customer opts into storage (we call this "persisted artifacts"). If you opt in, you control per-tenant retention windows via the Console.

- Data residency: Hosted Redwood API supports region pinning. We have US-only inference clusters (us-west-1 and us-east-1). We can commit to US-only processing and storage in your contract (subject to technical scoping).

- Retention: Console supports per-tenant retention down to 0 days; we can set a default 30-day retention for logs that contain PII. Separately, we can redact or token-map PII before writing logs.

- Support access / break-glass: We do not provide standing access to raw PII to support by default. Options we can offer:
  * Role-based RBAC with least-privilege roles (view-only, support-troubleshoot, emergency-unmask).
  * Break-glass workflow: engineer requests access via Console -> requires an approver (you can configure a list of FinSecure approvers connected via SSO) -> single-use time-limited access token issued. All break-glass sessions are fully recorded and immutable in the audit trail.
  * Optional server-side token masking: we can mask high-sensitivity fields pre-log using configurable regex/substitution rules.

- Logging & audit: We keep detailed access logs (who, when, reason, duration, scope) and can channel them to your SIEM or to an export bucket. Immutable audit retention default is 1 year, but we offer a 3-year add-on (complies with your 3-year ask).

Proposed next steps:
1) Marissa to provide a short draft of our Support-Auth Matrix and a sample break-glass flow (attached: Redwood_Support-Auth-Matrix.pdf).
2) Alex to confirm whether FinSecure will: (a) allow Redwood to process requests in a US-only region, and (b) accept a 30-day default retention for PII-containing logs with the option to request shorter windows per tenant.
3) If yes, we can schedule a 30-minute technical walkthrough with our infra security engineer (Ben) to validate SSO integration and session recording details.

If you prefer, Ben can join tomorrow morning for 30 minutes to go over SSO and the approval API.

Best,
Evelyn Hart
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Alex Rivera <alex.rivera@finsecure.io>
Cc: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 22 Jun 2027 09:11:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up from today's discovery — emergency support & data requirements

Alex — attaching the Support-Auth Matrix and a short technical note on the break-glass approval API. Highlights for LegalOps: 

- Break-glass flow: Support engineer opens a request in Console -> FinSecure approver receives an Okta push + email -> approver can approve with a one-click action which issues a limited-time access token (default 20 minutes). The token is single-use and scoped to the minimum data subset requested.
- Token masking: Our default server-side mask replaces full-value strings for sensitive fields with stable tokens (e.g., <PII_TOKEN_abc123>) so debugging is possible without exposing raw data.
- Export audit: Exports that include PII require an additional approval step; exports are hashed and watermarked and placed in a customer-owned S3 bucket when configured.

Marissa attached: Redwood_Support-Auth-Matrix.pdf (contains the approval roadmap) and a short API snippet for Okta SCIM integration.

Let me know what time works for Ben's walkthrough; we have 9–11am PT tomorrow free.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Solutions Engineering Manager, Redwood Inference

From: Alex Rivera <alex.rivera@finsecure.io>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: LegalOps <legal@finsecure.io>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 22 Jun 2027 15:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up from today's discovery — emergency support & data requirements

Thanks — we reviewed the attachments and those answers are helpful. A couple quick clarifications before we lock pricing and scope: 

1) Approver model: FinSecure requires two approvers for any break-glass that grants view-unmasked PII (one from Security, one from Legal). Can Redwood support a dual-approval workflow?
2) Export handling: For S3 exports that contain PII, Legal requires that exported files be encrypted with our KMS and that Redwood cannot retain keys. Can you confirm the export path supports customer-managed KMS?
3) Audit retention: We'll accept the 3-year add-on for immutable audit logs. Please provide an updated quote reflecting that line item.

If you can confirm (1) and (2) via email, we can push this into procurement next week. Also please include Ben on the Okta integration call so we can vet the SCIM/OAuth flows.

Best — Alex

---
FinSecure LegalOps will send a short questionnaire by end of week; please expect it.
